items.original_text: Filing step: File the ABC Type 42 premises-to-premises transfer application with the California Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control, attaching the signed CUA motion, the seller's license, and proof of the lease, and post the ABC notice at the premises for 30 days. What to say: Complete ABC's transfer application forms, attach the CUA motion showing Planning approval, the lease or proof of right to occupy, the seller's permit from CDTFA, and the entity formation documents. Pay the ABC transfer fee (approximately $1,000–$1,600 for a Type 42). Post the ABC notice in a front window at 995 Valencia for 30 consecutive days; the 30-day posting starts the public comment period. ABC will refer the application to SFPD and SF Planning for review; Planning will confirm the CUA, and Police will assess neighborhood impact. If the census tract is over quota (as tract 208.01 is), ABC may require a Public Convenience or Necessity finding from the Board of Supervisors, adding 1–3 months. Coordinate with Planning and the Board clerk if a PCN hearing is triggered.

items.original_text: Filing step: File the building permit application with DBI for tenant improvements and the change of use from Restaurant to Bar, and submit the DPH plan check application at the same time so Health can review the kitchen layout, finishes, and equipment in parallel with the building permit. What to say: The building permit must route to Planning for zoning review. Attach the CUA motion to the permit application so DBI and Planning see that the use is authorized. Submit full plans (architectural, mechanical for the hood if any, plumbing, electrical) stamped by a California-licensed architect. File the DPH plan check application with the same plans, menu, and equipment list. DPH will assign a plan reviewer and schedule a pre-final inspection at ~80% construction completion and a final inspection before issuing the Health Permit to Operate. The building permit fee depends on construction valuation; budget $800–$15,000. The permit review takes 2–4 months when routed to multiple departments.
